title: Restitution, Moral Issues and Money Matters

blocks.text: RESTITUTION: What is Restitution and how do we restitute? Restitution involves restoring to the owner all things taken by falsehood, confessing all lies told and bringing all those we have deceived into the true pictures of things. {{prv 6:30,prv 6:31,prv 28:13|Proverbs 6:30-31, 28:13}}, {{act 24:16|Acts 24:16}}, {{ez 33:14,ez 33:15,ez 33:16|Ezek. 33:14-16}}, {{2sm 12:1,2sm 12:2,2sm 12:3,2sm 12:4,2sm 12:5,2sm 12:6|2 Sam. 12:1-6}}, Phil.1, {{lv 6:1,lv 6:2,lv 6:3,lv 6:4,lv 6:5,lv 6:6,lv 6:7|Lev. 6:1-7}}. It is being willing to let the Lord expose and then heal painful areas of our past. God commands that restitution be made. Restitution leaves behind an indelible testimony with the one whom restitution is made, which when an unbeliever is involved becomes a means of preaching the gospel of Jesus Christ. When a delicate restitution is to be made involving a non Christian, undoing wrongs done against organizations, or those that affect marriage relationships, etc. much prayer and counseling from men of God may be required.

MORAL ISSUES: God"s standard does not change with time and His views have not change on the following: Adultery: What is adultery? Does it belong to the Old Testament period? {{ex 20:14|Exodus 20:14}}, {{1co 6:9,1co 6:10,1co 6:15,1co 6:16|1Cor. 6:9-10, 15-16}} it involves breaking solemn marriage vows and defiling the conjugal bed. Heb.13:4, {{prv 6:20,prv 6:21,prv 6:22,prv 6:23,prv 6:24,prv 6:25,prv 6:26,prv 6:27,prv 6:28,prv 6:29,prv 6:30,prv 6:31,prv 6:32,prv 6:33,prv 6:34,prv 6:35|Prov. 6:20-35}}

Fornication: What is fornication? Is virginity outdated? {{1co 6:13,1co 6:18|1 Cor. 6:13, 18}}a, {{eph 5:3|Eph. 5:3}}, Rom.12:2. The fact that fornication is a common practice does not make it acceptable to God. Keep yourself pure, no sex before marriage, and no sex with someone you are not married to.
Sexual Perversion: What does it mean? {{lv 18:22,lv 18:23|Lev. 18:22-23}}, {{rm 1:26,rm 1:27|Rom. 1:26-27}}. Remember Sodom and Gomorrah

Flirting: Flirting is defined as showing attention or affection without serious intentions or emotional commitment; love is too serious for play acting. Paul warned Timothy {{1tm 5:2|1Tim. 5:2}} don"t send out the wrong signals. {{rm 14:16|Rom. 14:16}}; {{eph 4:27|Eph. 4:27}}. Be wise; ensure you keep a safe distance from members of the opposite sex you are not convinced you are going to marry.
Danger of Moral Indecency God regards it as a waste of resources. {{prv 29:3|Prov. 29:3}} As a vow breaker, you are under a curse. {{is 54:5|Isa. 54:5}}, Mal.2:14

It desecrates the blood purchased property of Jesus and attracts destruction. {{1co 6:19,1co 6:20|1 Cor. 6:19-20}} It is a sin against one"s body. {{1co 6:18|1 Cor. 6:18}} It opens doorway for Satan"s attack. Eccl.10:8b. People may outwardly laugh at you yet inwardly admire you as a Christian who has the courage to stand up for their moral chastity.

God initiated marriage. {{gn 2:18,gn 2:24,gn 2:25|Gen. 2:18, 24-25}}. Marriage should be between a man and a woman. {{lv 18:22,lv 18:23,lv 18:24|Lev. 18:22-24}} homosexuality is an abomination to God, God detest sexual perversion. {{rm 1:26,rm 1:27,rm 1:28|Rom. 1:26-28}} A Christian should marry only one wife. 1 Tim.3:2, {{gn 2:18,gn 2:24,gn 2:25|Gen. 2:18, 24-25}}

cards.heading: 2. Why should we marry? We should marry for the following reasons and more: 1Cor.7:

blocks.text: To obey the commandment of God {{gn 1:28|Gen. 1:28}} For fellowship and partnership, it takes two to make "one flesh" Eccl. 4; 9-11, {{gn 2:18,gn 2:24,gn 2:25|Gen. 2:18, 24-25}}. For the propagation of the human race {{gn 9:1|Gen 9:1}} To satisfy creation and sexual desires that are good, holy, and legitimate but it can only be satisfied in marriage 1Cor.7:1-15
Courtship:
Courtship is a time for the man and woman of getting better acquainted and ascertaining whether or not they are prepared for marriage.

cards.heading: 4. What is the Bible approved way of getting engaged to be married as a Christian?

blocks.text: {{1sm 16:7|1 Sam. 16:7}}, {{gn 24:1,gn 24:2,gn 24:3,gn 24:4|Gen. 24:1-4}}, {{1ts 4:1,1ts 4:2,1ts 4:3,1ts 4:4,1ts 4:5,1ts 4:6,1ts 4:7|1Thess. 4:1-7}}. Ensure that you and your intending spouse have a common understanding of the key doctrines of the Bible. {{hb 6:1,hb 6:2|Heb. 6: 1-2}}; Petting, romance, sex, should be strictly avoided during courtship. {{prv 9:17,prv 9:18|Prov. 9:17-18}}, Heb.13:4.

Can a Christian marry a non Christian? A Christian should marry a Christian only. No marriage should be contracted with an unbeliever. 2 Cor. 6; 14-17, {{am 3:3|Amos 3:3}}, {{dt 7:3,dt 7:4,dt 7:5,dt 7:6|Deut. 7:3-6}}. Any marriage contracted outside of God"s plan will often give birth to troubles.

cards.heading: 7. Marriage done before becoming a Christian

blocks.text: When should a Christian marry? Discuss.
If you are already married to an unbeliever God can use you to bless your unbelieving partner. {{1co 7:14,1co 7:10,1co 7:11,1co 7:12,1co 7:13,1co 7:14,1co 7:15,1co 7:16,1co 7:17|1Cor. 7:14, 10-17}}

God initiated marriage. {{gn 2:24|Gen. 2:24}}. God is against divorce. Mathew 19:6, 5:32, {{ml 2:13,ml 2:14,ml 2:15,ml 2:16|Mal. 2:13-16}}. Putting away and remarriage constitute adultery. {{mk 10:11,mk 10:12|Mark 10:11-12}}. Only death should separate a couple. {{rm 7:2,rm 7:3|Rom 7:2-3}}, Love renders divorce irrelevant in marriage. {{1co 13:4,1co 13:5,1co 13:6,1co 13:7|1 Cor. 13:4-7}}

items: Money Matters:
The Bible does not condemn money but gives some safe guidelines on the attitude of a Christian towards money
Do not love money. {{1tm 6:6,1tm 6:7,1tm 6:8,1tm 6:9,1tm 6:10|1 Tim. 6:6-10}}. The remedy is contentment with what God has provide you
Do not be too preoccupied with searching for money at the expense of God. Mathew 6:33
Do not hoard Money. {{mt 6:19,mt 6:20,mt 6:21|Matthew 6:19-21}}, {{1tm 6:17|1Tim. 6:17}}. your financial strength has no bearing in heaven or hell.
Take note of the following. {{1tm 5:8|1 Tim. 5:8}}, {{ec 7:12|Eccl. 7:12}}
Do not worship money. Mathew 6:24, {{prv 11:28|Prov. 11:28}}. Money should not be your God. No idolater shall inherit the kingdom of God.
Do not live in debts as a way of life. The only Bible recommended debt is love. {{rm 13:8|Rom. 13:8}}

Remember you have been bought with a price {{1co 6:20|1 Cor. 6:20}}, your money is the property of your master. You are only a custodian {{1co 4:2,1co 4:3,1co 4:4,1co 4:5,1co 4:6,1co 4:7|1Cor. 4:2-7}}, {{dt 8:18|Deut. 8:18}}
Do not put your trust in money. {{1tm 6:17|1Tim. 6:17}}, {{ps 62:10|Psalm 62:10}}b
Do not be involved in extortion, bribery and corruption. {{is 33:15|Isa. 33:15}}.

blocks.text: Biblical Principles of Giving The following principles of giving should be observed:

OFFERING Throughout the bible, God encouraged us to bring offerings to Him which is different from the Tithe. Today we do not bring Sin, Burnt, Guilt offerings because Jesus has done it all for us. However we Still bring thanksgiving offering. It is an expression of gratitude to our God. More so, He is honored. {{ps 50:23|Ps 50:23}}

1. What is offering? {{dt 12:16|Deut. 12:16}} They are gift that you give to God in addition to your tithe. Endeavor not to come into God"s presences empty handed. {{dt 16:16|Deut. 16:16}}. Note that offering is mentioned together with tithes. While tithe opens the windows of heaven, offering determines how wide it should be opened. Luke.6:38. Your offering should be given prayerfully and systematically

items: Why do you give?
To demonstrate God"s love and follow his example. {{jo 3:16|John 3:16}}, God is the ultimate giver. {{dt 8:16|Deut. 8:16}}
It opens up an opportunity to receive from God. {{lk 6:38|Luke 6:38}}
It is an opportunity to sow a seed of help and bless someone. {{prv 14:21|Prov. 14:21}}
It is more blessed to give than to receive, avoid the trap of stinginess. {{act 20:35|Acts 20:35}} {{prv 11:25,prv 11:26|Prov. 11:25- 26}}, 2Cor. 9.6

blocks.text: 3. What do you give?

You can give your skill, time, prayers, money, etc. {{ex 35:4,ex 35:5,ex 35:6,ex 35:7,ex 35:8,ex 35:9,ex 35:10,ex 35:11,ex 35:12,ex 35:13,ex 35:14,ex 35:15,ex 35:16,ex 35:17,ex 35:18,ex 35:19,ex 35:20,ex 35:21,ex 35:22,ex 35:23,ex 35:24,ex 35:25,ex 35:26,ex 35:27,ex 35:28,ex 35:29,ex 35:30,ex 35:31,ex 35:32,ex 35:33,ex 35:34,ex 35:35|Exo. 35:4-35}}, {{act 3:1,act 3:2,act 3:3,act 3:4,act 3:5,act 3:6,act 3:7|Acts 3:1-7}}, Peter and John had no money but gave healing in the name of Jesus; Peter gave his boat for Jesus to preach in. {{lk 5:1,lk 5:2,lk 5:3|Luke 5:1-3}}, nothing is too small, no matter how small it will make a difference. {{lk 21:1,lk 21:2,lk 21:3,lk 21:4|Luke 21:1-4}}, {{jo 6:1,jo 6:2,jo 6:3,jo 6:4,jo 6:5,jo 6:6,jo 6:7,jo 6:8,jo 6:9,jo 6:10,jo 6:11,jo 6:12,jo 6:13|John 6:1-13}}

items: To whom do you give?
Spiritual Leaders {{gl 6:6|Gal. 6:6}}, Phil.4:15-19
The Less privileged. {{prv 19:17,prv 21:13|Prov. 19:17, 21:13}}
Fellow Christians. Rom.12:13, {{act 11:29,act 9:36,act 9:37,act 9:38,act 9:39,act 9:40,act 9:41|Acts 11:29, 9:36-41}}
How do you give?
Freely and cheerfully: {{prv 11:24|Prov. 11:24}}, {{2co 9:7,2co 9:8|2 Cor. 9:7-8}}. It attracts Gods favorable attention
Give generously: {{2co 9:6|2 Cor. 9:6}}
In proportion to, at times beyond your means: {{act 11:29|Acts. 11:29}}, {{2co 8:13|2 Cor. 8:13}} {{mk 12:44|Mark 12:44}}.
Give without publicity: Mathew. 6:1-4

blocks.text: TITHE INTRODUCTION: Should a Christian pay tithes? The answer is yes. There is a huge debate raging among Christians as to whether tithes should be paid or not. Besides, many Christians give very little and sometimes nothing at all to support the work of God.

1. What is the tithe? It is the giving a tenth of one's income as an offering to God. Abraham was the first man ever recorded in the bible to give tithes to God, {{gn 14:17,gn 14:18,gn 14:19,gn 14:20|Genesis 14: 17-20}}. Melchizedek was the priest of the Most High God. The bread and wine he offered to Abraham has a close resemblance to the Lord's Supper. ({{lk 22:14,lk 22:15,lk 22:16,lk 22:17,lk 22:18,lk 22:19,lk 22:20,lk 22:21,lk 22:22,lk 22:23|Luke 22: 14 -23}}) {{hb 7:1,hb 7:2,hb 7:3,hb 7:4,hb 7:5,hb 7:6,hb 7:7,hb 7:8,hb 7:9,hb 7:10,hb 7:11,hb 7:12,hb 7:13,hb 7:14,hb 7:15,hb 7:16,hb 7:17,hb 7:18,hb 7:19,hb 7:20,hb 7:21,hb 7:22|Hebrews 7: 1-22}} sheds more light on Melchizedek. He was the priest of the Most High God. He was the only one qualified to receive tithes from Abraham. All this happened before the law was established. There is no record of Abraham, who was at this time still called Abram, being told to give tithes to God, nor is any explanation given. Jacob gives us the second reference to paying tithes when he made a vow to God. {{gn 28:22|Genesis 28:22}} The biggest argument against paying tithes seems to be with its association with the law. {{lv 27:30,lv 27:31,lv 27:32|Lev 27: 30 - 32}} {{nm 18:21,nm 18:22,nm 18:23,nm 18:24,nm 18:25,nm 18:26,nm 18:27,nm 18:28,nm 18:29|Numbers 18: 21 - 29}} says tithes go towards supporting the Levites who in turn give part of it as an offering to the Lord.

items: Purpose of the Tithe
To support the work of God {{lv 27:30,lv 27:31,lv 27:32|Leviticus 27:30 - 32}}
To provide for his laborers (the Levites)
To support strangers, homeless or disadvantaged the fatherless, and widows. {{dt 26:9,dt 26:10,dt 26:11,dt 26:12|Deut 26:9-12}}.

blocks.text: Note the term 'first fruits' are mentioned in Deuteronomy. Indeed this is what tithes are. They are the first portions that we take out of our income and offer in gratitude to God. Give it in the support of the church and ministry.

3. The first fruits When God brought Israel into the land of Canaan the first city they took was Jericho. God told them not to touch any of the spoil. ({{js 6:17,js 6:18,js 6:19|Joshua 6: 17 - 19}}) It was the Lord's. It was the first fruits of battle. It was their tithe. The next city to fall was Ai. Here they were allowed to take as much spoil as they needed ({{js 8:1,js 8:2|Joshua 8: 1 - 2}}). They had paid their first fruits or tithes with Jericho, Hence the difference. {{ml 3:3,ml 3:4,ml 3:5,ml 3:6,ml 3:7,ml 3:8,ml 3:9,ml 3:10,ml 3:11,ml 3:12|Malachi 3: 3 - 12}} gives God's mind with regards to paying tithes 4. But what does the New Testament say about tithes Not a lot. In fact the only references to tithing in the New Testament are {{mt 23:23|Matthew 23:23}}, {{lk 11:42|Luke 11:42}}, {{lk 18:12|Luke 18:12}} and Hebrew 7: 5 - 9. The giving of the law helped to establish the importance of many of the unwritten truths already known by god-fearing men. But when Jesus brought us faith there is no longer the need for the supervision of the law. {{gl 3:23,gl 3:24,gl 3:25|Galatians 3: 23 - 25}}. In other words, the law was given to make things clear. Without the law we would not understand sin. Sin was around before the law but the law exposed it. The giving of tithes was also around before the law. Again the law helped in the establishing its importance and relevance. The law did not invent tithing, it only exposed it. We could say the same of sacrifice and obedience. 5. Why do we pay tithes? Abraham gave tithes to Melchizedek, King of Salem, at his return from battle. {{gn 14:20|Gen. 14:20}} Jacob also imitated his grandfather's piety. {{gn 28:22|Gen. 28:22}} Moses ordained that all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or fruit of the land be given to God. {{lv 27:30,lv 27:31,lv 27:32|Lev. 27:30-32}}. God commanded us to bring our tithes into His storehouse. Mall 3:10 6. How do we pay our tithes? A starting place for all of us is one tenth, nothing less than that. We must bring it into the house of God promptly and cheerfully {{2co 9:6,2co 9:7,2co 9:8|2 Corinthians 9: 6 - 8}} with all our hearts and gratefulness to God. It should be the first fruit. In other words, the first thing you pay, an offering to God is not subject to other bills and needs you have; remember He owns it all. Tithing is your act of worship to God. {{gn 4:1,gn 4:2,gn 4:3,gn 4:4,gn 4:5|Gen 4:1-5}} Pay the tithe to the church where the whole truth is preached, the church where you are being fed with the word of God.

items: Benefits of tithing
God will rebuke the devourer for your sake. {{ml 3:11|Mal. 3:11}}

blocks.text: 2. God will open the windows of heaven and pour His blessings more than you can accommodate. {{ml 3:10|Mal. 3:10}}
Unfaithfulness in the area of tithing can make a believer to lose heaven, because it is stealing from God directly. NOTE
